Dear Dean,

Thank you very much for your reply.

I was hoping for a solution that could use the app variable directly, rather than a file, to recreate a new app directory. Best wishes,

Laurent

Dear all,

I have the same issue. It happens mostly when there is a slow internet connection. The page must be reloaded than but all data then are lost.

Is there a parameter to set a higher timeout time?

The shiny webpage explain those reasons:

Your application suddenly goes grey and you see in your logs that the application was “killed”.
Possible Diagnosis: Each Application Instance has a size which corresponds to the amount of RAM (memory) that is allocated to it. If the amount of memory allocated to this application is exceeded, then the Application Instance could be shut down by shinyapps.

Remedy: There are two possible solutions:
Increase the size of the Application Instance.
Decrease the number of workers per Application Instance. Since each worker takes up additional RAM, you may find that lowering the “Max worker processes” to two or one would help keep each Application Instance’s memory usage down.

Kind regards,
Karl

> Hi Mike,
>
> I did get this to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, with help from Tareef and Chad. They were going to write up the process. However, in short:
>
> 1. Create a set of SSH keys on your local machine
>
> 2. Add the relevant key to your database server. I used ssh-copy-id for this. There are many tutorials online. I use Digital Ocean and this is a good start: https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-configure-ssh-key-based-authentication-on-a-linux-server
>
> 3. Upload both public and private SSH key into a directory accessible from your Shiny app. I initially had some reservations about uploading the private key, but after thinking about it the alternative is an SSH tunnel initiated through username/password which is just as insecure, maybe more. Effectively your Shiny app server needs the private key because it's really taking the place of your local machine when making the SSH tunnel.
>
> 4. Then I have the following code (change credentials as appropriate):
>
> # Load db connector library
>
> library("RMySQL")
>
> # Change permissions on SSH keys
>
> system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa.pub"))
> system(paste("chmod 600 /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa"))
>
> # Open SSH connection
>
> system(paste("ssh -v -f -N -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -i /path/to/ssh/keys/id_rsa -L 3306:localhost:3306 user@hostname sleep 20"))
>
> # Database query
>
> con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host='127.0.0.1', user='youDBUser', password='yourDBPassword', dbname='yourDBName')
>
> sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM database.tablename", sep="")
>
> queryResults <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
>
> dbDisconnect(con)
>
> Key things to remember here are the path to the SSH key, make sure the directory where the SSH keys are located is writable and your user has rights to change the permissions, make sure port 3306 is open on both machines.
>
> I think that's it. It took me a few attempts, with some rookie errors, but with Tareef and Chad's help we found success.

Karl, Jason, Ray,
I think each of you may be having a different issue potentially.   Unfortunately the symptoms you are describing may all sound similar/identical, but there may be different underlying reasons for why you are getting the grey screen.  Checking the Javascript Console, and taking a look at the logs of the application will help you diagnose most of the issues.  The only one that isn't quite captured in the logs today is when your instance runs out of memory.  We have it on our plate to try and find a way to make that clear, but if you have looked at everything else, please send us a link to your application with steps to reproduce the issue and we can check for that memory issue ourselves.

Ray,
It sounds like you may have an issue with having a fully qualified path in your application (w:/...).  You will need to put that file in your application directory (or in some sub-directory of it) and load it up as a relative path.

Jason,
It doesn't sound like there is enough information to find out what your issue is, but I would recommend you check out the output of shinyapps::showLogs() to see if you get an error message there. If you could include a link to your application, we may be able to see what is going on as well.

Karl,
I am presuming you have already read this article on performance tuning:
https://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps-io-performance-tuning/ .  If not, you should hopefully have a feel for the types of timeouts you can configure to tune your application.

Best,
Tareef

I have setup the RDS MySQL instance in amazon. I am able to connect from my local pc to amazon rds instance and display results, but when I deploy in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> . I get below error:
Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'mysqlrealtimeanalytics.csfwhddjumf9.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com <http://mysqlrealtimeanalytics.csfwhddjumf9.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com>' (110)

I tried below steps from below link nothing worked out.

https://www.rstudio.com/faq-items/how-do-i-give-access-to-my-rds-instance-for-an-application-i-have-deployed-on-shinyapps-io/ to add the shinyapps account id to aws

>From the above link mentioned in point 2 it is mentioned to go to Security Groups. When I go there I am getting below message
"Your account does not support the EC2-Classic Platform in this region. DB Security Groups are only needed when the EC2-Classic Platform is supported. Instead, use VPC Security Groups to control access to your DB Instances. Go to the EC2 Console <https://us-west-2.console.aws.amazon.com/ec2/home?region=us-west-2#s=SecurityGroups> to view and manage your VPC Security Groups. For more information, see AWS Documentation on Supported Platforms <http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-supported-platforms.html> and Using RDS in VPC <http://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_VPC.html>."

I tried to goto VPC Security Groups and I have selected the database as mentioned in point 5 : In connection type there is no EC2 Security Group there is no option to add the account id as well.

Please suggest am I in right direction please tell if anywhere am I going wrong.

Please check the attachments for my aws rds settings .

Thanks and Regards,
Naveen Srikanth D.
